subject: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2 evidence) - Elara Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@elara-health.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode requirements (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for Elara: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Key constraints you called out:
- PHI will be processed as part of the clinical notes ingestion and downstream model outputs.
- Your security/compliance team requires SOC 2 Type II evidence and a signed BAA before any production traffic.
- You prefer customer-managed networking (VPC peering) but are open to Dedicated if Private is too heavy initially.

Redwood recommendation (based on the above):
- Hosted API: Not compliant for PHI unless Elara is comfortable with vendor-hosted PHI and additional contractual controls — likely not suitable.
- Dedicated capacity: Good middle ground — isolated GPU pool, predictable throughput, and we can implement stricter data retention and access controls. Requires reserved capacity agreement.
- Private VPC / On‑prem: Highest control for network and encryption, suitable if your security/legal require zero vendor-hosted PHI. Longer lead time for deployment.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will share our SOC 2 Type II report and a draft BAA for your legal/security team to review (attached).
2) Please complete the security questionnaire — I attached the spreadsheet we discussed.
3) Schedule a technical deep‑dive with our infra team (Dylan) to map network/topology and any required audit evidence (logs, key management).
4) If Dedicated looks right, we can prepare a committed capacity quote and deployment checklist.

Attachments: SOC2_Type_II_Redwood_2024.pdf (redacted), BAA_draft_Elara_Redwood.docx, security_questionnaire_elara.xlsx

Would you be able to share an estimated timeline for legal review and whether your procurement team needs a formal quote? Happy to set up a follow-up slot this week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode requirements (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from our side: 

- Confirmed: we cannot put PHI on a vendor-hosted shared environment, so Hosted API is out.
- Our security team prefers Private VPC if contract/legal can be finalized within 8-10 weeks; otherwise Dedicated with strict contractual controls is acceptable.
- We'll review the SOC2 report and BAA draft; security will fill the questionnaire and return it to you by Friday (we have a sprint review this week).

Two asks: 
1) Can you summarize the difference in ETA and cost delta between Dedicated and Private VPC (top‑level ballpark)?
2) For Dedicated, we need a clear list of audit logs and retention periods you provide out-of-the-box.

I'll loop in procurement once we have the ballpark.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of IT — Elara Health
samir@elara-health.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode requirements (HIPAA/BAA, SOC2)

Hi Samir — great, thanks for confirming. Answers inline: 

1) ETA & cost delta (high-level):
- Dedicated: ETA 2–3 weeks for provisioning dry-run + config; 4–6 weeks to production depending on network approvals. Ballpark premium vs Hosted: ~25–40% higher unit cost due to reserved GPU capacity and isolation. Exact numbers depend on committed vCPU/GPU tier.
- Private VPC: ETA 6–12 weeks (more if on‑prem), higher one-time setup effort and networking approvals; operational costs similar to Dedicated once running but potential infra/setup fees.

2) Audit logs / retention (out-of-the-box capabilities):
- Request/response logs (redacted for PHI by default unless explicitly allowed), 90 days retention configurable.
- Admin access logs and IAM changes: 1 year retention.
- Billing and usage traces: 3 years.
We can provide exports (S3/secure bucket) and streaming to your SIEM (OEM connector). If you need longer retention for specific artifacts we can add that to the proposal.

Attached are the SOC2 Type II PDF and the draft BAA. Neha — can you pick this up for the questionnaire when it lands? Dylan — can we line up a 60m technical call next week; Samir, what times work for you?

Attachments: SOC2_Type_II_Redwood_2024.pdf, BAA_draft_Elara_Redwood.docx

Best,
Marissa
